paragraphs: Rav Menashya, his son, Eruvin 64a; Hyman says the correct reading is “of Difta,” as in Eruvin 43b according to Ein Yaakov.[^1][^2][^3][^4]

notes.text: מג: is a locator 43b, not a name Megifti; Eruvin is supplied contextually from the preceding סד.,64a. Neither locus is independently verified against a named edition.
ע״י is read contextually as Ein Yaakov in the reading formula, without fresh collation.
Gifta is supplied מגיפתי, while Difta is Hyman’s proposed מדיפתי correction. כשם is understood contextually as as at/as the name appears at; no Hebrew change is made.

The initial audit heading מדיפתי differs from supplied מגיפתי. The proposed emendation remains Hyman’s categorical instruction, not a new identity or place adjudication. Rav Menashya is explicitly titled and is his son.
